note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a PAK 9, 14, 1926 Act 3, 7; A06b PAK 9, 14, 1926 Act 3, 8; L05 PAK 14): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships (with major exceptions); a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: Generally applicable provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory unconditionally; by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Pakistan, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Pakistan for 12 months immediately prior to the application, as well as during 4 out of 7 years predating the 12-month period. ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required. Dual citizenship allowed with the United Kingdom and any other country that the Federal Government may specify ... The person acquiring a foreign citizenship (or is about to acquire) may relinquish Pakistan citizenship voluntarily, asking the government to release him. When Pakistan citizenship is not relinquished voluntarily in this situation, it lapses ipso facto. Provision does not apply to a female citizen of Pakistan who is married to a person who is not a citizen of Pakistan. Provision is not applied to persons who acquire citizenship in the following countries: UK, France, Italy, Belgium, Iceland, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Finland, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Switzerland, the Netherlands, USA, Sweden, Ireland, Bahrain and Denmark. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Pakistan to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a citizen other than by descent.; Person is born abroad to a citizen by descent. He/she needs to be registered at a Pakistan consulate or the citizen parent needs to be in the service of Pakistan at the time of the birth. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Pakistan. Unless born to a father who is a foreign diplomat and not a citizen of Pakistan, or the father is an enemy alien and the child is born in a place then under occupation by the enemy. ... No provision
